extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and other stakeholders in medical publishing
extracted.subtask_description: A viewpoint/preprint discussing the opportunities and challenges of integrating generative AI into the peer review process for medical publications, including potential impacts on review quality, efficiency, and policy. The page is intended to inform debate and identify key issues for adoption and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency, fairness, and effectiveness of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript raises concerns about "the efficiency, fairness, and effectiveness of the review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: The exponential growth in submissions and reviewer shortages have strained traditional peer review, prompting evaluation of whether new approaches (including GenAI) can preserve or improve these key properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer capacity and the problem of repeated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: "The surge in submissions has led to a shortage of qualified reviewers, slowing down the peer review process. The repeated review of rejected manuscripts not only increases costs but may also stifle research innovation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion focuses on reviewer availability, turnaround time, and the systemic cost/innovation impacts of multiple review cycles; solutions should address reviewer capacity and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI capabilities relevant to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI (GenAI) such as ChatGPT has "exceptional capabilities in feature learning and textual expression, allowing them to identify complex relationships within data without relying on pre-existing assumptions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider GenAI's technical strengths (feature learning, relationship identification, natural-language generation) and how these could be leveraged responsibly in review workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to enhance semi-automated peer review systems
rubrics_metrics.description: "GenAI present an opportunity to enhance semi-automated peer review systems, potentially addressing the current limitations in the peer review process and improving the efficiency and quality of medical publications."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals on whether and how GenAI integration could improve throughput, consistency, or quality while preserving scholarly standards; consider human-AI collaboration models (semi-automated) rather than fully automated replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and addressing of benefits and challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: "This viewpoint highlights the potential benefits and challenges of integrating GenAI into the peer review and identifies the key issues that need to be addressed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should enumerate and critically assess benefits (e.g., efficiency gains) and challenges (e.g., reliability, bias, ethical/legal concerns, accountability) and propose concrete mitigations or research priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint caution: unreviewed status and limits on clinical application
rubrics_metrics.description: The page contains a warning: "This is an unreviewed preprint... Preprints - unless they show as 'accepted' - should not be relied on to guide clinical practice or health-related behavior and should not be reported in news media as established information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or using content from preprints, require explicit recognition of unreviewed status and prohibit using findings to guide clinical decisions or definitive public reporting without peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint display and peer-review settings
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists author-selected preprint settings: who may peer review (Anybody / Editor-selected reviewers), when to display the preprint PDF (Anybody anytime / Logged-in users only / Title & abstract only / No one), and similar options for the accepted manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluation of preprint workflows should account for configurable visibility and review-access options; policies should ensure stability of preprint DOI/URL and transparency about chosen settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation guidance for preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: "Please cite this preprint only for review purposes or for grant applications and CVs (if you are the author)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline: restrict formal citation of preprints to contexts that acknowledge provisional status (review purposes, grant/CV), and prefer citing the final peer-reviewed version of record (VoR) when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and redistribution restrictions for in-review preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: The page states: "Authors and publisher expressively prohibit redistribution of this draft paper other than for review purposes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints under review may carry restrictive licenses; evaluation and reuse should respect authors' and publishers' redistribution limitations until final publication/licensing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement for open peer-review participation during review window
rubrics_metrics.description: "Readers with interest and expertise are encouraged to sign up as peer-reviewer, if the paper is within an open peer-review period (in this case, a 'Peer Review Me' button to sign up as reviewer is displayed above)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies or systems should facilitate community reviewer sign-up during open review periods and provide clear mechanisms (buttons, links) and guidance for outside reviewers; outside formal periods, alternative engagement (e.g., tweeting) is encouraged.
